note: Source 1 returned thirty rows and not one proper name: every row was a modifier on 'drum and bass artists' (best, top, liquid, female, polish, japanese). Source 2 returned no person at all — its highest music-specific rows were 'amen break' (6,300), 'sound system' (5,700) and 'jungle' (50,000), which is a genre boundary, not a canon. Source 3's People Also Ask rows were 'Who is the biggest DNB artist?', 'Who are some of the best drum and bass artists?', 'Is DNB a subgenre of EDM?' and 'Who are some famous bass drum players?' — the last one is about drum kits, which is how thin this SERP is. Source 4 is a 2022 snapshot (TicketFairy: Jam Thieves, Dunk, Camo & Krooked, Lens, Tom Finster, Sl8r, Iyre, Visages, Nia Archives, Alix Perez, Pyxis, The Caracal Project, Elipsa, Kimyan Law, Noisia) and names no founder. So for the third genre running every founder below comes from source 5, en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drum_and_bass. Source 6 ranks S.P.Y (10 sets), London Elektricity (9), Flava D (8), Nia Archives (7), Tim Reaper (7), Machinedrum (7), Krakota (7). GENRE ATTRIBUTION, stated because this is the guide the mistake was made in: source 5 names 'Original Nuttah' by Shy FX & UK Apache only in its soundtrack-appearances list, and places the record's own scene in jungle. It is not required here and is not in this list. Its home is media/jungle.json, where source 5 for jungle returned it directly.

required_records.title: Inner City Life
required_records.why: source 5's crediting sentence for the genre's arrival is about the album this single opens — "The earliest mainstream drum and bass releases include Goldie's album Timeless from 1995" — and Goldie is one of the five names in its list of early producers who shaped the sound. Timeless is named in the prose; this is the record that plays it

required_records.title: Shadow Boxing
required_records.why: source 5: "Early producers including 4hero, Doc Scott, LTJ Bukem, Goldie, and Grooverider began shaping the sound by stripping away elements of hardcore rave music and emphasising bass and complex drum patterns." Doc Scott is the second name in that sentence and this is the record the techstep section is built on

required_records.title: Music
required_records.why: third name in source 5's early-producers sentence, and the melodic pole the whole 1993-1996 argument needs at the opposite end from Shadow Boxing. Weak title match — the audit will find the word 'music' anywhere on the page — so the embed id is the half of this check that is actually doing work

required_records.title: Brown Paper Bag
required_records.why: source 5: "Roni Size & Reprazent's album New Forms (1997) won the Mercury Prize, signalling wider critical recognition." New Forms is named in the prose; this is the single that plays it, and the moment the genre stopped being an underground argument

required_records.title: Mystic
required_records.why: source 5 names exactly two liquid funk pioneers — "more melodic and accessible forms like liquid funk emerged, pioneered by artists such as High Contrast and Calibre" — and this is one of the two. The liquid section rests on this sentence

required_records.title: Parallel Universe
required_records.why: source 5's early-producers sentence opens with 4hero, and source 5 separately credits Marc Mac and Dego with founding Reinforced Records. Widely called the first drum and bass album.

required_records.title: Hot Right Now
required_records.why: source 5: 'In 2012, drum and bass achieved its first UK No. 1 single, Hot Right Now, by DJ Fresh.' A genre's first number one is not optional.

required_records.title: The Basement Track
required_records.why: source 5 names exactly two liquid funk pioneers; Calibre had a player and High Contrast had a mention, so the section made a claim with half its evidence audible.

known_gaps.title: S.P.Y; Flava D; Krakota; Machinedrum; Tim Reaper
known_gaps.why: catalogue-only, and by FIGURES.md that makes them differentiators rather than errors: the five most-played drum and bass names in 62,877 sets that no competing guide's canon list contains. S.P.Y at 10 sets is the highest-ranked real artist in the genre's catalogue slice and returns zero hits on the page. Recorded so the next pass does not re-derive them.

known_gaps.title: Incredible — M-Beat featuring General Levy, 1994
known_gaps.why: not a gap, a flag. This record is embedded on this page and is also a required record in media/jungle.json, where source 5 for jungle names it as the track that took jungle to the charts. Two guides playing the same 1994 record is defensible at the jungle-to-drum-and-bass hinge, but it is the exact seam where the Original Nuttah mistake was made, so it is written down rather than left for somebody to notice twice.

known_gaps.title: Pulp Fiction — Alex Reece; The Angels Fell — Dillinja; Machine Gun — Noisia; LK — DJ Marky & XRS; Silence Is Loud — Nia Archives
known_gaps.why: not gaps. All five are embedded on the page and none was returned by three sources or by source 5, so they are recorded here to stop a later pass reading their absence from the required list as an error. Noisia and Nia Archives each came back from two sources (source 4 and the catalogue), one short. They are the writer's judgement, which the algorithm does not overrule.
